Since necessary facility engineering parameters as well as stack emission data are not available, data from a "typical" coal gasification facility were used to compute air quality impacts from stack-released emissions during operation. Modeling assumtions and stack and emission data used in this study are presented in Table 1 (Appendix J) and were extracted from a proposed 250 million cubic feet per day coal gasification plant presented in the discussion draft of the Northern Great Plains Resource Program (Atmospheric Aspects Work Group Report), December, 1974. These emission data are below state and federal emission regulations. In addition, one year (November, 1971 through November, 1972) of onsite Colstrip wind speed, wind direction and atmospheric stability data as presented in the Colstrip Generation and Transmission Project Applicant's Environmental Analysis, Appendix B report are used in the analyses presented herein.
The majority of hydrocarbon emissions from a gasification complex are expected to be methane and would be a function of engineering and design. The level of non-methane hydrocarbons expected emissions is unknown at this time, but as gasification technology improves, hydrocarbon emissions should decrease. Assumptions relating to hydrocarbon emissions would be premature at this time and therefore these emissions are not addressed in this study.
